source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Correct. Sensors and power-management circuitry stay on the other boards; the main board contains:

\- ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 module
\- INA219 current monitor measuring the 3.3V rail
\- USB-C programming connector plus an LDO for standalone operation
\- All JST connectors for the power board, sensor board, display, PIR, touch inputs, LEDs, buttons, and reset
\- Supporting components including decoupling capacitors, pull-ups, series resistors, Schottky diodes, and a BOOT button

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The count is 14 JST connectors, with an additional on-board USB-C; most have low pin counts.

value_updates.general_pin_count_characteristic: most JST connectors have low pin counts

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: By low pins, I was referring to every connector except the interboard ones.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The power board is no problem, so could you instead add a 2-pin JST-GH connector to the main board for a panel-mounted power button? PWRON already arrives through J\_PWR\_SIG pin 4; the new connector only needs to tap that line so a button can be wired from the enclosure panel.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: From the main board, only these two connections go to the sensor board: J\_SENSOR\_PWR, using a 4-pin JST-PH at 2.0mm, and J\_SENSOR\_SIG, using a 6-pin JST-GH at 1.25mm.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
My rough calculation gives a 140×100 board an area of 14000mm², with the components occupying about 5200mm², or ~37% coverage. That still seems comfortably within normal PCB density and should route cleanly on 8 layers.

Rather than consolidating everything into a 2x24+12p, I'd like to retain the individual JST connectors. The modular arrangement matters for the enclosure: every sensor gets its own clean cable, and the boards slide into rails. A single large connector feeding a fan-out ribbon cable would leave the enclosure wiring messy and difficult to service.

Because the components are already placed in KiCad, could you resize the outline to 140×100 and make a rough rearrangement? I am not proficient with KiCad, so what would take me hours should take you minutes with the complete project already open. I would really appreciate you trying the resize on your side.

Keeping the ESP32 on the edge is fine.

value_updates.connector_architecture: retain individual JST connectors rather than a consolidated 2x24+12p connector
